keyVerseText: The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six.
rootMeaning: The name אֲדֹנִיקָם (ʼĂdônîyqâm) derives from the Hebrew words אָדוֹן (ʼâdôwn), meaning 'lord' or 'master,' and קוּם (qûm), meaning 'to arise' or 'to rise.' Thus, its root meaning conveys the idea of 'my lord has arisen' or 'lord of rising,' suggesting a figure of authority who has come into power or prominence. This literal sense enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing not only lordship but also a dynamic action of rising or establishing authority, which may symbolize restoration or new beginnings.
usageInScripture: The word אֲדֹנִיקָם appears three times in Scripture, consistently referring to the name of an Israelite family head, specifically a clan leader who returned from exile. It is uniformly translated as 'of Adonikam,' indicating possession or descent, which highlights its use as a proper name rather than a common noun. This consistent usage underscores its role as an identifier of a distinct family group within the post-exilic community, emphasizing heritage and continuity.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אֲדֹנִיקָם as 'my lord has arisen' invites reflection on God's sovereign action in raising leaders and restoring His people, especially after exile. The name embodies the faith that God is actively involved in the history of Israel, raising up individuals and families to fulfill His purposes. For the Christian faith, this points forward to the ultimate Lord who has risen—Jesus Christ—who restores and leads His people. Recognizing the name's meaning encourages believers to trust in God's providential leadership and the hope of renewal through Him.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 2:13 states, 'The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty and six,' identifying a significant number of descendants linked to this family leader. The inclusion of the name Adonikam here emphasizes the continuity of God's people through their families even after exile, highlighting God's faithfulness in preserving His covenant community. The meaning 'my lord has arisen' enriches this verse by reminding readers that the restoration of Israel is under divine lordship and blessing.
